texts: In the book's description of surgery for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, an incision of the ventricular wall below the commissure between the left and right coronary cusps is the step that is not part of the repair: B.
The myectomy, the sculptor's block, is begun through the aortic valve beneath the nadir of the right coronary cusp, and the trough is extended toward the apex when the obstruction lies low.
When the LAD runs under a muscular bridge it can be unroofed, the brick bridge lifted off the lad's slide, and the mitral valve is replaced when it cannot be repaired.
Memory hook: a block from the biceps, a trough toward the tip, a bridge lifted and a spare mitre; Usopp's chalk line is crossed out.
